programServices.description: Membership program: The Guild provided members with access to a fully equipped woodworking facility, shared tools and equipment, and member benefits including storage, library resources, and participation in Guild activities. Membership dues revenue supported ongoing facility operations and member services throughout the year.

Woodworking education programs: The Guild conducted woodworking skills education classes (account 4002, $50,217) and woodworking safety education courses (account 4003, $5,800) for members and the public. Expenses include instructor fees, materials, and event costs for skills and safety education programming (accounts 5001 and 5002, $38,495 and $2,902 respectively, plus conferences/meetings line $18,137).

Facility operations and ancillary programs: The Guild operated a shared woodworking facility providing rent income, storage, library services, merchandise sales, program events, and other program income to members. Expenses include shop equipment, maintenance, supplies, raffle, library, A/V, and other program costs supporting facility-based member services.

scheduleO.narrative: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild Inc. is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization incorporated in Missouri in 1992. Its mission is to promote the art and craft of woodworking by providing members with access to a shared workshop facility, woodworking tools and equipment, skills education classes, safety training, program events, library resources, and storage. The Guild fosters a community of woodworking enthusiasts through member programming, fundraising events, and educational outreach.

Membership program expenses of $159,575.75 include rent expense (account 5005, $150,000) and shop facilities maintenance (account 5015, $9,575.75) directly supporting the Guild's member facility operations. Membership dues revenue of $171,525 was recognized during the year; deferred membership dues at year-end totaled $59,130 (account 2212).

Woodworking education program expenses of $59,534.02 include skills education expenses (account 5001, $38,495.35 including merchant fees $2,954.70), safety education expenses (account 5002, $2,901.74 including merchant fees $320.00), program events expenses (account 5003, $12,567.28 including special events $10,008.89), and membership program expenses (account 5010, $5,569.65 including merchant fees $3,844.70). Revenue includes skills education $50,217, safety education $5,800, and program events $7,995.39.

Facility operations and ancillary program expenses of $51,103.35 include remaining 5000-series program expenses not separately detailed above, including shop equipment expense (5013, $2,239.71), shop equipment maintenance (5014, $6,013.37), shop supplies (5016, $5,315.25), merchandise expense (5004, $4,841.30), raffle expense (5006, $830.00), library expense (5008, $96.00), A/V equipment (5009, $709.45), and other program costs. Revenue includes rent income $26,016, storage income $7,231.57, library income $176.17, assets sold $2,782.60, other program income $5,266.56, and program events $7,801.23.

The organization conducted raffle activities (account 4007 Woodworking Raffle Sales) generating gross receipts of $2,548.00, classified as unrelated business income. The organization has filed or will file Form 990-T for the tax year ended December 31, 2025, as required. Raffle expenses (account 5006) totaled $830.00.

The organization received non-cash contributions (gift-in-kind) totaling $4,589.67 (account 4012 Woodworking Gift-In-Kind Income) during the tax year. These contributions consisted of donated woodworking materials, tools, or supplies used in Guild programming.

Prior to filing, a copy of Form 990 is provided to the Board of Directors for review. The Treasurer prepares the return and distributes it to all board members for review and comment before submission to the IRS.

The organization makes its governing documents, conflict of interest policy, and financial statements available to the public upon written request directed to the Treasurer at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO 64108-1121. The organization's Form 990 is also available through the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search database.

No other changes in net assets were recorded during the tax year. The change in net assets of $44,959.00 represents the excess of total revenue ($364,652.76) over total expenses ($319,693.76) for the year ended December 31, 2025. Beginning net assets of $407,394.93 plus the excess of revenue over expenses of $44,959.00 equals ending net assets of $452,353.93.

The organization qualifies as a public charity under section 509(a)(2) based on its receipt of more than one-third of its support from membership fees, program service revenue, and contributions from the general public related to its exempt woodworking education and community programming functions. The five-year support schedule reflects 2025 data only; prior year detail was not available from source systems for 2021-2024. The organization should confirm public support percentage with its tax preparer using complete five-year data.

The number of voting members of the governing body (7) and independent voting members (7) are estimated based on officer and director names identified in QuickBooks credit card account holders (John Steyer, Chuck Saunders, Gary Mielke, Richard Higgason) and standard Guild governance structure. The preparer should confirm the exact number of board members serving during 2025.

The organization relies substantially on volunteer labor to conduct its programs and operations. The estimated 50 volunteers reflects active member volunteers contributing to Guild programming, facility maintenance, education instruction, and event coordination. No employees were compensated during the tax year.
